headline: Govt employees to get salary hike of 100-142% under new pay scale
summary: The cabinet has approved a new national pay scale for civil servants and armed forces, to be implemented in three phases starting from July 1.
details: The cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has approved a new national pay scale for civil servants and the armed forces. Basic salaries will increase by 100% to 142%, depending on the grade.

The new pay scale will be implemented in three phases over two years. According to the Finance Division, 40% of the basic salary increase will be effective from July 1, 2026, followed by 30% in January 2027 and the final 30% in July 2027.
Under the new structure, the basic salary for the lowest (20th) grade will rise from 8,250 BDT to 20,000 BDT, while the highest (1st) grade will increase from 78,000 BDT to 156,000 BDT.
A separate pay scale for the judiciary will be developed by a dedicated committee. Pensioners will also benefit, with increases ranging from 55% to 100% based on their current pension amount.
The government will implement the 'one grade, one pension' system gradually by 2030 to avoid sudden financial pressure. In the meantime, an alternative arrangement has been made for pensioners.
New benefits include a monthly allowance of 3,000 BDT for children with special needs and a mobile allowance for all grades, expanding from the previous restriction to grade 5 and above.

Approximately 3.3 million people, including 2.4 million active employees and 900,000 retirees, will benefit from this move. The government expects an additional annual cost of approximately 105,580 crore BDT.
caption:
Basic salaries for government employees are set to jump by 100-142%!

The cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has approved a new national pay scale for civil servants and the armed forces. Basic salaries will increase by 100% to 142%, depending on the grade.

The new pay scale will be implemented in three phases over two years. According to the Finance Division, 40% of the basic salary increase will be effective from July 1, 2026, followed by 30% in January 2027 and the final 30% in July 2027.

Under the new structure, the basic salary for the lowest (20th) grade will rise from 8,250 BDT to 20,000 BDT, while the highest (1st) grade will increase from 78,000 BDT to 156,000 BDT.

A separate pay scale for the judiciary will be developed by a dedicated committee. Pensioners will also benefit, with increases ranging from 55% to 100% based on their current pension amount.

The government will implement the 'one grade, one pension' system gradually by 2030 to avoid sudden financial pressure. In the meantime, an alternative arrangement has been made for pensioners.

New benefits include a monthly allowance of 3,000 BDT for children with special needs and a mobile allowance for all grades, expanding from the previous restriction to grade 5 and above.

Approximately 3.3 million people, including 2.4 million active employees and 900,000 retirees, will benefit from this move. The government expects an additional annual cost of approximately 105,580 crore BDT.

headline: 3 Air Force personnel killed in road crash at Dhaka airport's 3rd Terminal
summary: A pickup truck lost control and plunged from a flyover at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, leaving three dead and four others injured.
details: Three members of the Bangladesh Air Force were killed and four others were injured in a road accident at the Third Terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Monday night.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the accident occurred around 10:20 PM when an Air Force pickup truck lost control and plunged from a flyover on the second floor of the Third Terminal.
The deceased personnel have been identified as Warrant Officer Mahmud, Corporal Piyas, and LAC Zubaidul.
Immediately following the crash, the injured members were transported to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Dhaka for necessary medical treatment.
The deceased were also moved to CMH for further proceedings.
